ACNJ explorer
Denver, Colorado85 contributions

Really good and authentic food
May 2026 • Couples
We stayed next door to this place and being westerners we were a little intimidated by its small quarters, thinking it was just for locals. So we gingerly got our foot in the door by grabbing a beer during an afternoon rain shower. The family was so kind to us, offering a couple of pop up seats out of the rain and a bowl of delicious peanuts to help the beer go down. They’ve got a great selection of brews so you’re bound to find one you like. I was particularly fond of the blonde. 
As luck would happen we did a food tour the next day and our first stop: yup, Tue An! We snuck in thru the ground floor shop to a hidden door leading up to the A/C cooled room upstairs where we tucked into banh cuon nong that was absolutely delicious. This may just be our breakfast option for the next two days. It’s ridiculously good. 
We came back later in the day during another rain shower for a beer and then finished our night out later in the evening with one last beer to do some fabulous people watching before calling it a (very successful) night! 
Please visit Tue An - your taste buds will love you for it.

Our hearts are full: Leaving Hanoi with the lesson that the best things in life don’t need to be fancy 🇻🇳✨
May 2026 • Couples
Our hearts are full: Leaving Hanoi with the lesson that the best things in life don’t need to be fancy 🇻🇳✨

We woke up hungry and headed out for a stroll around Hoan Kiem Lake, with absolutely no plan for breakfast. 

We were just wandering, letting the city wake us up, when we caught a scent that changed everything.

A deep, savory, simmering all night aroma drifted across the street. We followed the steam and found a small, bustling shop packed with locals. 

Our hearts told us to go for it, and it was the best decision of our entire trip. We stumbled upon Quán Tuệ An, and it was exactly the hearty, soulful meal we needed.

The Breakfast Spread

• Phở Tim Cật (Heart & Lung Noodle Soup): A true local’s choice. The broth was crystal clear but incredibly deep in flavor, the perfect "wake up" for the palate.

• The "Dim Sum" Style Rolls: We ordered both the Bánh Cuốn Nóng (freshly steamed rice rolls) and the Trứng Cuốn (egg rolls). Watching them steam these right in front of us made them taste even better! silky, light, and topped with a mountain of crispy shallots.

• Fresh Soya with Silken Tofu: My husband’s favorite! The freshest soy milk we’ve ever had, served with cloud-like scoops of soft tofu. It balanced the savory soup perfectly.

The Space: Humble & Homey

The place is small, but they make it work effectively! Don't expect a massive, spacious hall, it’s a classic, humble Hanoi shop.

• Downstairs: You get to be right in the action with the steam and the cooking.

• 2nd Floor: If you want more leg room and the comfort of Air Conditioning, head upstairs! It’s very homey and comfortable. We honestly couldn't ask for more.

Why They Deserve the Spotlight

The family running this is so accommodating and nice, you can tell they put their heart into the service. They even have a "Phở Treo" (Suspended Pho) board where you can pay forward a meal for someone in need.

As much as I want to "gate-keep" this spot so it stays our little secret, they truly deserve the recognition. It’s a shop with a soul.

📍 Honest Review & Info:

• Place: Quán Tuệ An (since 1987)
• Address: 14B Bảo Khánh, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội
• Price: Unbeatable quality.
• Beef Pho: 50,000 VND
• Steamed Rice Rolls: 35,000 VND
• Egg Rolls: 15,000 VND
• Soya with Tofu: 20,000 VND

Moral of the story: If you’re strolling near the lake and you smell something incredible, follow it. Sometimes the best memories are the ones you didn't plan for. 🇻🇳❤️ xoxo
